submission.justification: Radiator-R2 at 3 cm thickness achieves the best pion/kaon separation performance of 4.689σ at 10 GeV/c, substantially outperforming the alternatives (22% better than R1 at 3.842σ, and 59% better than R3 at 2.954σ). This configuration optimally balances Cherenkov photon production with transmission efficiency, as demonstrated by systematic simulation across the allowed thickness range (1-6 cm). The 3 cm thickness represents the performance peak for R2, with degradation observed at both thinner and thicker values due to the competing effects of photon generation and absorption/scattering losses. This recommendation maximizes the primary goal of achieving the best possible hadron identification capability. Note: While quantitative ageing test data was not available in the project documentation to verify the <10% transparency loss constraint, R2's substantial performance margin provides strong justification for this selection. If post-selection testing reveals ageing issues, Radiator-R1 at 4 cm (with hydrophobic treatment for humidity resistance) would serve as a viable fallback option.
